newsitem.title: UK: Gilt interest payments to be made gross - BOE.
newsitem.headline: Gilt interest payments to be made gross - BOE.

text.p: As part of the British budget, all gilt interest will be payable without deduction of withholding tax, although investors who wish to continue to receive net dividends will be able to do so, the Bank of England said on Wednesday.
The new measures will come into effect from April 6, 1998.

"The quarterly accounting arrangements for gross gilt interest received by UK taxable companies will remain in place for interest on those gilts to which quarterly accounting at present applies," the Bank of England said in a statement.
"But quarterly accounting will not apply to interest on future new gilt issues unless HM Treasury directs at the time a new gilt is issued that it is to apply to interest on that gilt."
The Bank said the measures would enable the abolition of those existing arrangements under which gilt interest is already paid gross.
These include the CGO star account arrangement, introduced on January 2, 1996, to facilitate the gilt repo market, allowing companies and British exempt bodies to receive gilt interest gross.

The CGO gross scheme, the CGO double taxation agreement scheme and the E arrangement were set up to cater for other means of receiving gross gilt interest, in particular for those investors entitled to exemption on the FOTRA (Free of Tax to Residents Abroad) gilts or to relief under double taxation treaties.

"The major simplification...will thus substantially reduce the tax compliance burdens of custodians and others, making the gilt market more accessible and attractive to investors and thus helping to reduce the cost of future public borrowing," the BoE said.
It said a transitional provision would ensure that existing holders of gilts who currently received net interest would not be affected by the change unless they chose to switch to gross payment.

The Bank said before the changes came into effect its registrar's department would write to all registered gilt holders offering those who currently received net interest the choice of gross payment if they so wished.

"Holders of gilts within CGO who currently receive net interest will be offered the opportunity to change to gross payment for some or all of their membership accounts and designations," the BoE said.

The quarterly accounting mechanism was introduced on January 2, 1996 in tandem with star accounts. Under it, companies liable to British income tax which choose to receive gilt interest gross would have to account for tax on the gilt interest they receive.
Interest on gilts which are to be strippable has been payable gross since June 7 1997.
